description: Every provider asked for Boat's machine, 4 vCPU and 8 GB, or its nearest size.

rows.name: Daytona
rows.note: Daytona's container sandboxes have no pause: stop and start restarts the sandbox and ends every running process.

rows.name: Upstash Ephemeral Box
rows.note: Upstash Ephemeral Box has no pause and resume

rows.name: Boat
rows.note: Boat has no pause: stop and start restarts the machine and ends every running process.

rows.name: Vercel Sandbox
rows.note: Vercel Sandbox's pause keeps files but not processes: pause stops the session, and resume starts a new one from the saved file system, ending every running process.

rows.name: Modal
rows.note: Modal sandboxes can't stop and run again, so Modal has no pause and resume

rows.name: Baseten
rows.note: no pause call. A sandbox goes on standby by itself about 15 s after its last request, keeping its memory, files and running processes, and the next request resumes it. Only its resume is timed, so it isn't ranked as a pause + resume total: the first command after standby took 0.21 s (median of 100, after 30 s with no requests).

rows.name: Beam
rows.note: Beam sandboxes have no pause and resume (Beam's persistent VMs do; they are a different product and weren't tested)
